11007-jemmy-stubbins-or-the-nailer-boy-i.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I was suddenly diverted from my contemplation of this magnificent scenery, by a fall of heavy rain drops, as the prelude of an impending shower. Seeing a gate open, and hearing a familiar clicking behind the hedge, I stepped through into a little blacksmith's shop, about as large an American smoke-house for curing bacon.

arxiv-2003-05232.title: Spin Seebeck Effect near the Antiferromagnetic Spin-Flop Transition
arxiv-2003-05232.creator: Derek Reitz, Junxue Li, Wei Yuan, Jing Shi, Yaroslav Tserkovnyak
arxiv-2003-05232.description: Abstract We develop a low-temperature, long-wavelength theory for the interfacial spin Seebeck effect (SSE) in easy-axis antiferromagnets. The field-induced spin-flop (SF) transition of Néel order is associated with a qualitative change in SSE behavior: Below SF, there are two spin carriers with opposite magnetic moments, with the carriers polarized along the field forming a majority magnon band.

arxiv-2101-03156.title: Topological line in frustrated Toric code models
arxiv-2101-03156.creator: M. H. Zarei, J. Abouie
arxiv-2101-03156.description: Abstract Typical topological systems undergo a topological phase transition in the presence of a strong enough perturbation. In this paper, we propose an adjustable frustrated Toric code with a ”topological line” at which no phase transition happens in the system and the topological order is robust against a non-linear perturbation of arbitrary strength.

arxiv-2104-05685.title: A vector leptoquark interpretation of the muon g − 2 g-2 and B B anomalies
arxiv-2104-05685.creator: Mingxuan Du, Jinhan Liang, Zuowei Liu, Van Que Tran
arxiv-2104-05685.description: Abstract We show that a single vector leptoquark can explain both the muon g − 2 g-2 anomaly recently measured by the Muon g-2 experiment at Fermilab, and the various B decay anomalies, including the R D ( ∗ ) R_{D^{(*)}} and R K ( ∗ ) R_{K^{(*)}} anomalies which have been recently reported by the LHCb experiment.

arxiv-2104-06460.title: A Co - Operative Game Theoretic Approach for the Budgeted Influence Maximization Problem Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2104-06460.creator: Suman Banerjee
arxiv-2104-06460.description: Abstract Given a social network of users with selection cost, the Budgeted Influence Maximization Problem ( BIM Problem in short) asks for selecting a subset of the nodes (known as seed nodes ) within an allocated budget for initial activation to maximize the influence in the network.

arxiv-2111-15620.title: Bayesian Level Set Approach for Inverse Problems with Piecewise Constant Reconstructions Journal: Inverse Problems
arxiv-2111-15620.creator: William Reese, Arvind K. Saibaba, Jonghyun Lee
arxiv-2111-15620.description: Abstract There are several challenges associated with inverse problems in which we seek to reconstruct a piecewise constant field, and which we model using multiple level sets. Adopting a Bayesian viewpoint, we impose prior distributions on both the level set functions that determine the piecewise constant regions as well as the parameters that determine their magnitudes.

arxiv-2304-06398.title: A Logical Account of Subtyping for Session Types
arxiv-2304-06398.creator: Ross Horne, Luca Padovani
arxiv-2304-06398.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ross Horne, Luca Padovani. We study the notion of subtyping for session types in a logical setting, where session types are propositions of multiplicative/additive linear logic extended with least and greatest fixed points. The resulting subtyping relation admits a simple characterization that can be roughly spelled out as the following lapalissade: every session type is larger than the smallest session type and smaller than the largest session type.

arxiv-2310-16558.title: A multiplicity formula for the Milnor number of smoothable curves
arxiv-2310-16558.creator: Andrei Benguş-Lasnier, Terence Gaffney, Antoni Rangachev
arxiv-2310-16558.description: Abstract . For a reduced complex analytic curve germ we introduce an algebraic invariant we call the complete intersection discrepancy . We determine some of its basic properties. As an application we derive a multiplicity formula for the Milnor number of a reduced smoothable curve singularity generalizing a well-known formula due to Lê, Greuel and Teissier for complete intersection curves.

arxiv-2311-16331.title: Helioseismic Investigation of Quasi-biennial Oscillation Source Regions Facilities: GONG
arxiv-2311-16331.creator: Kiran Jain, Partha Chowdhury, Sushanta C. Tripathy
arxiv-2311-16331.description: Abstract We studied the temporal evolution of quasi-biennial oscillations (QBOs) using acoustic mode oscillation frequencies from the Global Oscillation Network Group. The data used here span over more than 25 yr, covering solar cycles 23 and 24 and the ascending phase of cycle 25.

arxiv-2404-00737.title: Interaction-driven breakdown of Aharonov–Bohm caging in flat-band Rydberg lattices
arxiv-2404-00737.creator: Tao Chen, Chenxi Huang, Ivan Velkovsky, Tomoki Ozawa, Hannah Price, Jacob P. Covey, Bryce Gadway
arxiv-2404-00737.description: Abstract Flat bands play a central role in hosting emergent states of matter in many condensed matter systems, from the nascent insulating states of twisted bilayer graphene to the fractionalized excitations found in frustrated magnets and quantum Hall materials. Here, we report on the experimental realization of highly tunable flat-band models populated by strongly interacting Rydberg atoms.

arxiv-2412-11914.title: The Erdős unit distance problem for small point sets
arxiv-2412-11914.creator: Boris Alexeev, Dustin G. Mixon, Hans Parshall
arxiv-2412-11914.description: Abstract We improve the best known upper bound on the number of edges in a unit-distance graph on n n vertices for each n ∈ { 16 , … , 30 } n\in\{16,\ldots,30\} . When n ≤ 21 n\leq 21 , our bounds match the best known lower bounds, and we fully enumerate the densest unit-distance graphs in these cases.

arxiv-2508-15356.title: ε \varepsilon -Stationary Nash Equilibria in Multi-player Stochastic Graph Games
arxiv-2508-15356.creator: Ali Asadi, Léonard Brice, Krishnendu Chatterjee, K. S. Thejaswini
arxiv-2508-15356.description: Abstract A strategy profile in a multi-player game is a Nash equilibrium if no player can unilaterally deviate to achieve a strictly better payoff. A profile is an ε \varepsilon -Nash equilibrium if no player can gain more than ε \varepsilon by unilaterally deviating from their strategy.

arxiv-2509-21479.title: Filtering with Confidence: When Data Augmentation Meets Conformal Prediction
arxiv-2509-21479.creator: Zixuan Wu, So Won Jeong, Yating Liu, Yeo Jin Jung, Claire Donnat
arxiv-2509-21479.description: Abstract With promising empirical performance across a wide range of applications, synthetic data augmentation appears a viable solution to data scarcity and the demands of increasingly data-intensive models. Its effectiveness lies in expanding the training set in a way that reduces estimator variance while introducing only minimal bias.

arxiv-2510-19016.title: Modeling the Optical Colors of Galactic Cirrus Clouds in the Stripe 82 Region
arxiv-2510-19016.creator: Kwang-Il Seon, Jongwan Ko, Woowon Byun, Jaehyun Lee, Young-Soo Jo
arxiv-2510-19016.description: Abstract Observations have shown that the optical colors of Galactic cirrus clouds differ significantly from those of extragalactic sources; thus, they can be used to distinguish Galactic cirrus from extragalactic low surface brightness (LSB) features. To understand these properties, we calculate radiative transfer models in dust clouds, where photons are incident from the ambient interstellar medium (ISM).

pmc-10624908.title: Structural basis for the toxicity of Legionella pneumophila effector SidH
pmc-10624908.creator: Rahul Sharma, Michael Adams, Simonne Griffith-Jones, Tobias Sahr, Laura Gomez-Valero, Felix Weis, Michael Hons, Sarah Gharbi, Rayene Berkane, Alexandra Stolz, Carmen Buchrieser, Sagar Bhogaraju
pmc-10624908.description: Legionella pneumophila (LP) secretes more than 300 effectors into the host cytosol to facilitate intracellular replication. One of these effectors, SidH, 253 kDa in size with no sequence similarity to proteins of known function is toxic when overexpressed in host cells.

pmc-10631739.title: Impact of Holocene environmental change on the evolutionary ecology of an Arctic top predator
pmc-10631739.creator: Michael V. Westbury, Stuart C. Brown, Julie Lorenzen, Stuart O’Neill, Michael B. Scott, Julia McCuaig, Christina Cheung, Edward Armstrong, Paul J. Valdes, José Alfredo Samaniego Castruita, Andrea A. Cabrera, Stine Keibel Blom, Rune Dietz, Christian Sonne, Marie Louis, Anders Galatius, Damien A. Ford
pmc-10631739.description: The Arctic is among the most climatically sensitive environments on Earth, and the disappearance of multiyear sea ice in the Arctic Ocean is predicted within decades. As apex predators, polar bears are sentinel species for addressing the impact of environmental variability on Arctic marine ecosystems.

pmc-11508933.title: Genome-Wide Association Study for Seed Yield of Tepary Bean Using Whole-Genome Resequencing
pmc-11508933.creator: Waltram Ravelombola, Aurora Manley, Hanh Pham, Madeline Brown, Caroline Ruhl, Protik Ghosh
pmc-11508933.description: Tepary bean (Phaseolus acutifolius A. Gray) is a diploid legume species (2n = 2x = 22). It is the most drought- and heat-tolerant crop of the genus Phaseolus. Tepary bean is native to the northern part of Mexico and the south-western part of the U.S.

pmc-12105731.title: Drifting plasmons in two-dimensional electron channels: circuit analogy
pmc-12105731.creator: O. Sydoruk
pmc-12105731.description: Plasmons in two-dimensional electron channels have potential applications in the terahertz frequency range. Equivalent circuit models provide a convenient framework for analysing the plasmons. This article introduces a circuit model for plasmons in the presence of a dc current that flows in a gated channel.

pmc-12549506.title: The ChinaSTAD Chinese Registry in Patients with Moderate-To-Severe Atopic Dermatitis Not Controlled by Topical Therapy: Baseline Characteristics, Disease Burden and Treatment
pmc-12549506.creator: Ping Liu, Bingjiang Lin, Yanna Shen, Yonghong Lu, Jingyi Li, Dong Lv, Xu Yao, Xiaoyong Man, Hong Fang, Guan Jiang, Nan Yu, Dongmei Liu, Siyan Zhan, Jianzhong Zhang
pmc-12549506.description: IntroductionIn China, real-world evidence on the burden and management of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD) is needed. The ChinaSTAD study aimed to characterise the treatment and disease and health economic burden of patients with moderate-to-severe AD uncontrolled on topical therapy in China.

pmc-12584044.title: Management Approach to Obstructive Jaundice in Pregnancy due to Gallstones at the Milton Cato Memorial Hospital, St Vincent and the Grenadines: A Case Study
pmc-12584044.creator: Afia Boko Ampe Asare, Francis Dwomoh, Barry Aussi, Immanuel Olarinde, Divine Amakhu Dele, Franké Joseph, Stephanie Providence, Kwame Adu Okyere Boadu
pmc-12584044.description: Obstructive jaundice in pregnancy, though rare, can result from hormone‐induced biliary stasis and gallstone formation. Prompt recognition and timely surgical intervention, such as cholecystectomy and bile duct exploration, are critical to preventing maternal and fetal complications. This case highlights the need for vigilance in managing biliary disorders during pregnancy.

pmc-12820247.title: A statistical approach to model soil microbiota versus heavy metals: a case study on soil samples from Foggia, Southern Italy
pmc-12820247.creator: Alessandro De Santis, Antonio Bevilacqua, Maria Rosaria Corbo, Barbara Speranza, Matteo Francavilla, Giuseppe Gatta, Federica Carucci, Milena Sinigaglia
pmc-12820247.description: Heavy-metal (HM) contamination undermines soil functions and food safety, while risk appraisals often rely on chemical indices that can be unstable in the presence of extremes and only indirectly reflect biological integrity. We present an integrative framework that couples standardized contamination metrics with soil microbiome profiling to deliver stable, interpretable classifications and actionable bioindicators.

pmc-12966426.title: PRDM1 restricts bladder cancer progression and enhances chemosensitivity by suppressing OTUD6A-mediated deubiquitination of CDC6
pmc-12966426.creator: Jianfeng Cui, Shouzhen Chen, Xiaochen Liu, Xuewen Jiang, Guangzhou Cheng, Zhifeng Liu, Hui Zhao, Yaofeng Zhu, Benkang Shi, Yongxin Zou
pmc-12966426.description: PR domain zinc finger protein 1 (PRDM1) functions as a critical transcriptional repressor. The role of PRDM1 in various tumors is controversial, and its specific mechanism in bladder cancer (BCa) remains unclear. In the present study, we demonstrated that PRDM1 expression is downregulated in both human BCa tissues and BBN-induced mouse models of BCa.

pmc-13106753.title: High-frequency turbidity by sensors as a proxy for total phosphorus: implications of sampling strategies on the water framework directive classification
pmc-13106753.creator: Eva Skarbøvik, Anastasija Isidorova, Maria Kämäri, Pasi Valkama, Sofie G. M. van’t Veen, Emma E. Lannergård, Jens Fölster, Brian Kronvang
pmc-13106753.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mean concentrations of pollutants and nutrients are frequently used in the classification of water bodies under the European Commission Water Framework Directive. Turbidity can be used as a proxy for several particle-associated substances. We used three years of sensor turbidity data in each of 10 Nordic streams to assess the uncertainty in the annual arithmetic mean concentration of turbidity when sampling weekly, fortnightly, or monthly.

pmc-13286781.title: Glioma identification from microRNA biomarkers using machine learning
pmc-13286781.creator: Rakesh Kanth Andugala, Alyson Cieslik, Maria Braoudaki, Iosif Mporas
pmc-13286781.description: Gliomas are the most aggressive malignant brain tumours, occurring mostly in adults and accounting for approximately 80% of central nervous system malignant tumours. pmc-13606653.title: Effect-Allele Frequencies at Cardiometabolic Risk Loci in an Uzbek Cohort from Tashkent: A Central Asian Reference and Priorities for Polygenic Score Validation
pmc-13606653.creator: Alisher A. Abdullaev, Darya V. Zakirova, Sergei A. Kosushkin, Fazliddin Z. Xonboev, Guzal J. Abdullaeva, Rano B. Alieva, Shahlo U. Turdikulova
pmc-13606653.description: Background/Objectives: Central Asian populations are almost entirely absent from genomic reference resources, yet Uzbekistan has one of the fastest rates of growth in age-standardised type 2 diabetes (T2D) incidence. Allele frequencies at cardiometabolic risk loci are unknown, limiting the interpretation of polygenic risk scores (PRS) derived elsewhere.
